chunks: Al-Hasan ibn Mahbub, from Abi Ayyub, from Sulayman ibn Khalid, from Abi Abdillah عليه السلام:

A man came to the Prophet صلى الله عليه وآله and had struck a pregnant woman, causing her to miscarry a stillborn fetus. Then the woman’s husband came to the Prophet صلى الله عليه وآله and sought redress against him, and he said:
The assailant said: O Messenger of Allah, it neither ate nor drank, nor did it cry out, nor scream, nor show any sign of life. So the Prophet صلى الله عليه وآله said: “Indeed, you are a rhyming man.”
Then he ruled concerning it that a slave be given.

key_terms.اَلضَّارِبُ: the assailant; the one who struck the pregnant woman
key_terms.حُبْلَى: pregnant; describing the woman who was struck
key_terms.رَقَبَةً: a slave; the compensation ruled in this case
key_terms.سَجَّاعَةٌ: one who speaks in rhymed prose; a rhetorical rebuke to the speaker’s style
key_terms.سِقْطًا مَيِّتًا: a stillborn fetus; the unborn child expelled dead
key_terms.فَأَسْقَطَتْ: she miscarried; indicating the loss of the fetus due to the assault
key_terms.فَاسْتَعْدَى: he sought redress; the husband requested judgment against the assailant
key_terms.فَقَضَى: he ruled; indicating the Prophet’s legal judgment

ai.seo_question: What did the Prophet صلى الله عليه وآله rule in the case of a pregnant woman struck until she miscarried a dead fetus?
ai.summary: This hadith relates a legal case brought before the Prophet صلى الله عليه وآله concerning a pregnant woman who was struck and miscarried a dead fetus. The Prophet صلى الله عليه وآله rejected the assailant’s rhetorical defense and issued a legal ruling imposing compensation, showing the seriousness of harm done to the unborn.
